editorial:
Imagine waking up in 1974 South Korea to news of a shocking shooting that everyone is pretending didn't happen. You get to follow three very different guys: Cheol-gu, a cop who saw the whole thing go down; Jae-hwan, a grumpy editor fighting his bosses; and Young-il, a new reporter just trying to make a name for himself. The vibe is tense and gritty, making you feel like you are right there in the smoky offices and dark alleys of the seventies. It starts as a mystery but quickly turns into a dangerous game of cat and mouse as these three team up to find out who is really pulling the strings behind the scenes.

What really hits home is how the acting feels so real, especially the chemistry between the cop and the reporters. The action scenes are punchy and don't drag on too long, though some parts of the middle feel a bit slow. If you love stories about uncovering government secrets, you will love this. You should definitely watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the cool period details, or just rent it on Apple TV for a movie night. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a great move.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out the shooting was actually ordered by the highest levels of the government to kill a political rival. The three main characters manage to leak the evidence to the public, but it comes at a cost. Cheol-gu has to go on the run to avoid being framed, while the reporters lose their jobs. It ends on a bittersweet note, showing that while the truth got out, the system is still hard to change.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves political conspiracies and gritty detective stories.
